Jordan / Lauren — thanks for the ping. Draft redlines attached (OrderForm_SKY-3243_redlines.docx). High level recommendations:

1) Invoice cadence: Agree to pilot split 70% invoiced on delivery (due on receipt) and 30% invoiced 45 days after invoice date (Net45). We should mark the second tranche as "subject to collection" and not accelerate other obligations.

2) Tax reserve: Add a 5% tax reserve clause — Redwood will withhold 5% of the initial invoice amount where local law or customer request indicates potential withholding. The reserve will be released within 10 business days of receipt of valid tax residency evidence (tax certificate or equivalent).

3) Invoicing fields: Require PO number and remit-to email on face of invoice. Add a clause that invoices without a valid PO or correct remit-to may be returned and deemed not received for purposes of payment timing.

4) Escrow/holdback: Rather than formal escrow, recommend a holdback line-item (the 5% reserve) on the invoice to avoid escrow account complexity for a pilot. If Finance needs escrow we can escalate.

Operational caveats: Lauren / Ben, please confirm the mechanics (GL code, holdback accounting) — if Finance would prefer Net30 with a 30-day hold for the retained portion, flag now.

I’m attaching the redline and a one-paragraph summary you can send to Skyforge. If they sign off we can push a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
